faq.a: Enter your current pay and a raise percent, and the calculator works out your new hourly, weekly, monthly, and annual pay. Or enter your new pay amount instead, and it works out the percent change for you.
faq.q: How do I use this calculator?

faq.a: Yes. Enter your current pay and your new pay amount, leave the raise percent blank, and the calculator shows the percent change between them.
faq.q: Can I work out the percent of a raise I already got?

faq.a: Conversions use a 40 hour week and 52 weeks a year. If you work a different schedule, your real weekly and annual pay will differ, so treat the converted figures as a standard full-time comparison.
faq.q: What work schedule do the conversions assume?

faq.a: No. The figures are gross pay before taxes and deductions. Your take-home pay after a raise will be lower, and a higher income can also move you into a higher tax bracket for the extra dollars.
faq.q: Is this my take-home pay after the raise?

sources: No external figure is used on this page. The 40 hour week and 52 week year are stated conversion assumptions, not sourced data.

title: Pay Raise Calculator | ToolVerse
whenNotToUse: Conversions assume a 40 hour week and 52 weeks a year. They will not match a part-time or irregular schedule.
It shows gross pay only. Taxes, retirement contributions, and other deductions are not included.
It does not account for overtime, bonuses, or commissions.
